lab_title: Anatomy of the Human Heart: Chambers, Valves, Vessels, and Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart.
Locate the four major valves and explain their role in preventing backflow.
Recognize the major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through pulmonary and systemic circulation.
Relate left ventricular wall thickness to its role in systemic circulation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart’s position, orientation, and major external vessels as a foundation for deeper internal anatomy.
key_visuals: A 3D human torso with the heart highlighted in the mediastinum
An external view of the heart showing apex, base, and great vessels
Color cues distinguishing deoxygenated and oxygenated blood pathways
student_actions: Rotate and inspect the heart in anatomical position
Identify the apex and base
Locate the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, pulmonary trunk, pulmonary veins, and aorta

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students identify the four chambers and distinguish right-sided from left-sided blood flow roles.
key_visuals: A cutaway heart model revealing right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle
Color-coded right and left sides of the heart
Labels indicating chamber names and relative wall thickness
student_actions: Select each chamber on the model
Match each chamber with whether it receives or pumps blood
Compare the ventricular walls visually

scenes.brief_purpose: Show the location of the four valves and demonstrate how they maintain one-way blood flow.
key_visuals: Close-up views of the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves
Animated valve opening and closing during a simplified cardiac cycle
Arrows showing normal forward blood movement and blocked backflow
student_actions: Tap each valve to reveal its name and connected chambers or vessels
Sequence the valves in the order blood encounters them
Observe which direction each valve permits flow

scenes.scene_name: Right Heart to Lungs: Pulmonary Circuit
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace deoxygenated blood from the body through the right side of the heart to the lungs.
key_visuals: Animated flow entering from the superior and inferior vena cava into the right atrium
Movement through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle and through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary arteries
A linked lung model showing blood heading toward gas exchange
student_actions: Follow the pathway step by step
Place pathway markers in the correct order
State where blood is deoxygenated and where it is headed next

scenes.scene_name: Left Heart to Body: Systemic Circuit
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace oxygenated blood from the lungs through the left side of the heart and out to the body.
key_visuals: Animated return through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium
Flow through the mitral valve to the left ventricle and through the aortic valve into the aorta
A body map showing systemic distribution
student_actions: Reconstruct the pathway from lungs to body
Differentiate pulmonary veins from pulmonary arteries
Identify where oxygenated blood enters and exits the heart

scenes.scene_name: Why the Left Ventricle Is Thicker
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect heart structure to function by comparing ventricular myocardium and pressure demands.
key_visuals: Cross-sectional comparison of right and left ventricular wall thickness
Pressure arrows indicating shorter pulmonary versus longer systemic circulation
A simplified pump analogy showing differing force requirements
student_actions: Compare the two ventricles visually
Predict which ventricle generates greater force
Explain why the left ventricular myocardium is thicker

scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize chamber, valve, vessel, and circulation knowledge into one complete blood-flow sequence.
key_visuals: A full heart-and-lung circulation overview with interactive labels hidden or minimized
Movable tokens representing blood cells
Mixed prompts involving chambers, valves, and vessels
student_actions: Trace a full drop-of-blood journey from body to body
Correctly name each structure in sequence
Identify errors in an intentionally incorrect flow pathway
